evidence: Receiving DO2 observations t=46.2-52.0 h: sustained 1.0-1.7 mg/L, below minimum_do_mg_l=2.0
Source batches never fell below ~7.4 mg/L DO2 at matched times, indicating receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit
Delayed P assay: receiving 2.57 g/L at 48 h vs source 2.98-3.06 g/L

Forward model comparison: strong_feed_reduction gives lowest below-limit hours (10.4), lowest oxygen deficit (8.76 mg·h/L), highest min DO (0.81 mg/L), highest product mass (128.74 kg) among all actions
Model estimated transfer multiplier 0.40, indicating source-calibrated model substantially overpredicts receiving DO capacity; relative action ranking still favors the 0.6-feed/1.15-air intervention
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~46.2 h to 1.0-1.7 mg/L, well below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen operating minimum, and has stayed there for ~6 h — an active constraint violation that KEEP would perpetuate. Source batches never dropped below ~7 mg/L at comparable times, confirming a receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.40). Of the bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (feed ×0.6, air ×1.15) is the best trade-off: the forward model shows it yields the fewest below-limit hours (10.4 vs 13-17.4 for other actions), the smallest post-decision oxygen deficit (8.76 vs 11.4-13.3 mg·h/L), the highest minimum DO, and the highest retained product mass (~128.74 kg). Reduce_feed or increase_air alone address only one side of the oxygen balance; the strong combined action attacks both oxygen demand and supply. A stop is rejected because it zeroes counted production. Although the source-calibrated model is imperfect and predicts no action fully restores DO ≥ 2.0 mg/L, strong_feed_reduction dominates the relative ranking on every oxygen and mass metric.
args.uncertainty: The physical forward model is calibrated on source batches with an estimated transfer multiplier of 0.40, so its absolute DO predictions likely underestimate the receiving vessel; its predicted absolute infeasibility under all actions should not be taken as truth. The relative ranking favoring strong_feed_reduction is more robust. There is residual uncertainty in hidden receiving parameters (OUR kinetics, Kla) — the strong feed cut may slow production rate somewhat, but model runs show no product-mass penalty vs alternatives, and mass is volume×concentration preserved. One extra assay was available but the online DO2 trace already gives decisive, timely evidence of the oxygen violation; a 4-h-turnaround assay would not change the intervention choice.
